turns.replyText:
I've been disappointed by similar products before, so quality really matters to me.

I hear you. When you’ve been let down before, it makes sense to be extra careful about what you buy next.

A few things about how we handle quality at Heirloom:

We grow our roses ourselves as premium own-root roses at our nurseries in Oregon, not from outside suppliers.
Perennials and roses are grown in containers (not bare root) so you get an established plant with a developed root system.
Everything is inspected and defoliated before shipment so it travels well, and you’ll get it in soil, ready to plant.
Roses are covered by a one-year guarantee, and perennials by a 90-day guarantee, so you’re not on your own if something doesn’t perform.

To make sure we pick the right thing for you, can you tell me:

Are you looking for a rose, another perennial (like hydrangea, lavender, etc.), or bulbs?
Your ZIP code or hardiness zone?
What the planting spot is like: full sun (6+ hours) or partial shade (about 4+ hours), and whether it’s in the ground or a container?
The one or two traits that matter most to you (for example: strong fragrance, great for cutting, compact size, very low maintenance, specific color)?

Once I have those, I can narrow it down to options that are both high quality and a good match for your conditions, so you don’t waste money or effort.
